content:
maria: Kicking off network bring-up for the new eu-north GPU cluster (gpu2 pool). Need a quick review + pair for validation tomorrow morning. Main concerns: TGW peering to core transit, BGP session limits, private hosted zone delegation for service discovery, and egress NAT cost sizing.

ajay: I can join for the validation at 09:30 CET. Quick Q — are we using per-account NAT gateways or centralised NAT in the transit account?

maria: Central NAT in transit account to keep egress IPs stable for allowlists. We'll route 10.200.0.0/16 through the TGW attachment and rely on route propagation.

shelby: Reminder: central NAT will add cross-account data transfer charges. We should estimate 1.5TB/month per GPU node at peak for checkpoint pulls. Can we gate to HS caching in eu core?

maria: Good call. We'll enable prefix caching on the model store and set aggressive cache TTLs to reduce egress. Also adopting instance lifecycle hooks to warm cache on scale-up.

networking-oncall: Checklist I want validated during handoff: 
- TGW attachment status (rt-prop enabled)
- Propagated routes include VPC CIDR and pod-cidr ranges
- BGP sessions (if using TGW-Transit with TGW appliances) up and stable
- Private Hosted Zone delegation to account route53 (ns entries propagated)
- Security group/NACLs allow control-plane CIDRs and kube nodes
- NAT gateway scaling plan and smoke test for SNAT persistence
- Egress monitoring & billing alarms

chris: For the TGW routes: run this in the transit account to confirm propagation: 
```bash
aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --filters Name=transit-gateway-id,Values=tgw-0abc12345 
# then check propagation status 
aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-table-propagations --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-0abc12345
```

ajay: I'll verify the TGW RTB propagation and post results. Also will validate that the route priority for pod egress is correct (we want prefer local VPC for intra-region, TGW for cross-region).

maria: DNS plan: create private hosted zone dev.internal.redwood and create NS glue records in core account for eu-north delegation to the cluster account's route53. Ensure resolver rules in the VPC point to the route53 inbound endpoints in core for cross-account resolution.

shelby: Small gotcha — inbound resolver endpoints are regional. For cross-region resolution we need forwarding rules or resolver endpoints in each region. Confirming whether core has eu-north resolver.

maria: Core has resolver in eu-core and eu-north? I think only eu-core. If missing, we'll deploy an inbound endpoint in eu-north in the transit VPC and create a resolver rule in the cluster VPC.

ops-bot: deploy bot: PR 4872 merged — created TGW attachment, route table, and IAM role for cross-account route propagation.

chris: After TGW checks, run BGP health check (if using appliances) or do a traceroute to the model store prefix to confirm path: 
```bash
# from a bastion in cluster VPC
traceroute -n 10.50.12.5 
# from transit bastion to core model store IPs
traceroute -n 52.18.22.33
```

ajay: Results: TGW propagation incomplete for two pod CIDR prefixes (10.200.128.0/18 and 10.200.192.0/19) — propagation shows pending. Raised a quick ticket, looks like the attachment was created before the route table association. Re-associated and propagation kicked off.

maria: thanks. After propagation completes, we should run the kube egress smoke: curl model-store.internal:8080/health from a sample node, then curl an external IP to validate NAT SNAT IP is the transit NAT IP.

shelby: Also validate that long-lived connections (gRPC streaming) maintain IP stability across NAT scaling events. We had an incident where NAT scaling caused ephemeral port churn. Test with 30m persistent stream.

networking-oncall: Cost control items to confirm before handoff:
- Billing alarm for cross-account data transfer > 500GB/day
- Per-VPC egress tagging so billing export can map to customer/team
- Confirm reserved NAT capacity vs autoscale limits (we cap to avoid runaway costs)

maria: For GPU provisioning notes: minimum 3 GPU2 nodes to start (kube autoscaler min=3), prefer instance types g5.2xlarge for evaluation. We'll attach node-labels and taints for high-memory workloads. Please ensure the cluster SGs allow egress to quay/github for image pulls but restrict 0.0.0.0/0 access for control-plane.

ajay: Pairing tomorrow @09:30 CET. Before that I'll: 
- confirm TGW propagation all green
- run traceroutes and post outputs
- validate resolver endpoints and route53 delegation TTLs
- run kube egress smoke + 30m gRPC stream test

maria: Sweet. After successful validation we'll do handoff to eng-oncall: provide runbook with recovery steps: detach TGW attachment, revert route propagation, fallback to local NAT per-VPC (if needed).

tarek: Add one more thing — manifest the route53 change in infrastructure repo so infra-as-code reflects delegation and inbound rule. Saves manual drift.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a follow-up PR with the delegation records. Handoff checklist will include links to PRs, the TGW IDs, transit NAT EIP list, and the egress billing alarm ARN.

networking-oncall: OK — please paste the TGW ID and the transit account NAT EIP(s) here once available and mark this thread with :white_check_mark: when ready for oncall takeover.

maria: TGW ID is tgw-0e9f1a2b3c and transit NAT EIP(s): 3.125.45.66, 3.125.45.67. PRs: infra#523 (route53 delegation), infra#524 (tgw attachment autoscript). Marking as ready for validation tomorrow.

ops-bot: reminder: please add runbook entry under ops/runbooks/networking/eu-north-gpu.md (template created).

chris: I'll be on-call for the night window. If propagation doesn't converge within 10 minutes post-association, escalate to aws-network-support.

maria: Thanks team. Posting a short runbook summary in the PR and will ping again after the validation run. :rocket:
